Module 01: Orientation — Learning Objectives

By the end of this module, students will be able to:

  • Explain the Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) commit model of Git and how distributed version control functions as an immutable audit trail for collaborative textual scholarship.
  • Execute foundational command-line Git workflows (staging, committing, branching, and conflict resolution) applied directly to multi-witness transcription files.
  • Distinguish between Unicode Canonical Decomposition (NFD) and Canonical Composition (NFC) in polytonic Greek textual encodings and explain why normalization is mathematically required for computational search and collation.
  • Diagnose and resolve character encoding anomalies, decomposed diacritical clusters, and non-standard Greek sigla in digital textual corpora.
